a: In June 2008, three members of Fitwatch were found guilty of obstructing FIT officers who were trying to photograph people attending a No Borders meeting in London. The following year, in July 2010, the Inner London Crown Court reversed the men's convictions, and the judge observed that the FIT officers may have infringed the protesters' human rights.
h: Three members of Fitwatch were convicted for obstructing FIT officers in June 2008 as they attempted to photograph those attending a No Borders meeting in London . In July 2010 the Inner London Crown Court overturned the men 's convictions , with the judge stating that the protesters ' human rights may have been violated by the FIT officers .

a: Contemporary writing on typography takes a firm stance on the matter. Ilene Strizver, who founded the Type Studio, argues, "Forget about tolerating differences of opinion: typographically speaking, typing two spaces before the start of a new sentence is absolutely, unequivocally wrong." The Complete Manual on Typography (2003) declares that "the typewriter tradition of separating sentences with two word spaces after a period has no place in typesetting," describing the single space as "standard typographic practice." Likewise, The Elements of Typographic Style (2004) recommends a single space between sentences, remarking that "your typing as well as your typesetting will benefit from unlearning this quaint [double spacing] Victorian habit."
h: More recent works on typography weigh in strongly . a: A key contribution Innis made to communications studies was applying the concepts of time and space to different media. He classified media as either time-binding or space-binding. Time-binding media are long-lasting and include clay or stone tablets, whereas space-binding media are more transient and encompass modern forms such as radio, television, and mass circulation newspapers.

a: Common cold and atypical pneumonia: One hundred CPS men took part in experiments in which they inhaled or drank throat washings taken from soldiers suffering from colds and pneumonia. This work demonstrated that colds and certain forms of pneumonia are caused by a virus rather than by bacteria.
h: Common cold and atypical pneumonia : A hundred CPS men participated with tests such that they inhaled or drank throat washings from soldiers with colds and pneumonia . This research proved that colds and some types of pneumonia are cause by a virus , not bacteria .

a: Nathan was called up to the San Francisco Giants on April 20, 1999, filling the roster spot vacated by star slugger Barry Bonds, who was placed on the disabled list following surgery on his left elbow. h: Other proteins that serve structural functions are motor proteins such as myosin , kinesin , and dynein , which are capable of generating mechanical forces . a: During the Iron Age, a Celtic language and culture took shape in Ireland. The question of how and when Ireland became Celtic has been a subject of debate for nearly a hundred years, and the migrations of the Celts remain among the most persistent topics in archaeological and linguistic research. At present, scholars hold more than one view on how this transition came about in Ireland.
h: During the Iron Age , a Celtic language and culture emerged in Ireland . How and when the island of Ireland became Celtic has been debated for close to a century , with the migrations of the Celts being one of the more enduring themes of archaeological and linguistic studies . Today , there is more than one school of thought on how this occurred in Ireland .

a: Proteins are not completely rigid structures. Beyond the levels of structure already described, they can move between several related forms as they carry out their functions. When discussed in terms of these functional rearrangements, the tertiary or quaternary structures are typically called "conformations," and the shifts between them are known as conformational changes. Such changes are frequently triggered when a substrate molecule binds to an enzyme's active site, the part of the protein where chemical catalysis takes place. In solution, proteins also experience structural variation due to thermal vibration and collisions with other molecules.
h: Proteins are not entirely rigid molecules . In addition to these levels of structure , proteins may shift between several related structures while they perform their functions . In the context of these functional rearrangements , these tertiary or quaternary structures are usually referred to as " conformations " , and transitions between them are called conformational changes . Such changes are often induced by the binding of a substrate molecule to an enzyme 's active site , or the physical region of the protein that participates in chemical catalysis . In solution proteins also undergo variation in structure through thermal vibration and the collision with other molecules .

a: Determining exactly how many aerodromes support general aviation in the UK is difficult. The Pooleys 2008 United Kingdom Flight Guide records 355, while the Airplan Flight Equipment UK VFR Flight Guide 2008 records close to 500. Lockyears Farm 'Strips' and Private Airfields Flight Guide identifies more than 300 landing sites. The GASAR study puts the figure at 1,100 formal flying sites in England alone, including 400 sites that are known to planning authorities but absent from flight guides. It further estimates an additional 759 informal sites known only to landowners, customs officials, and members of the enthusiast organisation Air-Britain.

a: Thomas Vincent Darden (born August 28, 1950) is a former American football cornerback, safety, and punt returner who spent his career with the Cleveland Browns of the National Football League (NFL). During his time in the NFL, he was named All-Pro free safety on three occasions and was selected to the Pro Bowl in 1978. He holds most of the Cleveland Browns' franchise records for interceptions. He was also an All-American defensive back for the Michigan Wolverines football team and recorded one of the most memorable interceptions in the history of college football. After his playing days ended, Darden worked as a sports agent, a security provider, and a business consultant.

a: By the spring of 1794, the French Atlantic fleet was scattered even more widely than its British counterpart. Rear-Admiral Pierre Vanstabel had been sent out with five ships, two of them ships of the line, to escort the badly needed French grain convoy off the eastern coast of America. Rear-Admiral Joseph-Marie Nielly had departed Rochefort with five ships of the line and a number of cruising warships to meet the convoy in the mid-Atlantic. As a result, Villaret was left with 25 ships of the line at Brest to counter the threat presented by the British fleet commanded by Lord Howe.
